data.label: Support staff (browser)
data.description: Support agents using a browser. This is a caller, not a provisioned resource.

data.label: Staff sign-in
data.description: Handles staff authentication and supplies the group claims used to filter retrieval. Whether a tenant already exists is unconfirmed.

data.label: Staff assistant app
data.description: The staff interface. It shows the ticket, customer context, a draft answer with citations and an Escalate button. Staff must approve before anything is sent.

data.label: Assistant orchestration API
data.description: Uses a managed identity. Pulls the ticket, reads the CRM record (read-only), runs permission-filtered retrieval, calls the model and applies the grounding check. It has no refund or CRM-write tools. The draft response with citations is returned to the app.

data.label: Synthetic ticket queue
data.description: Existing synthetic support tickets. The integration method is to be confirmed.

data.label: Existing CRM (customer records)
data.description: Customer records, read-only from the assistant. Writes and refunds are excluded by design. The API and access scope are to be confirmed.

data.label: Approved knowledge store
data.description: Private container holding only approved knowledge articles, each with access-group metadata.

data.label: Authorized retrieval index
data.description: Indexes the approved knowledge. Queries are filtered by the staff member's groups, so unknown groups return nothing. Keyword, vector or hybrid mode is still open.

data.label: Answer drafting model
data.description: Drafts answers only from retrieved passages and must cite sources or abstain. The model, deployment, quota and regional availability are unverified. Local tests use scripted responses.

data.label: Grounding & safety check
data.description: Checks the draft for groundedness, harmful content and prompt injection. Ungrounded drafts and any refund or record-change request are sent to escalation.

data.label: Human escalation queue
data.description: Escalated tickets with reason and context, handled by a senior agent. Refunds and CRM changes are always done by a person.

data.label: Audit & monitoring
data.description: Traces, the audit trail of retrievals, drafts and escalations, and alerts. Log retention is to be agreed.

discovery.problem: Assist support staff with grounded, authorized answer drafts. Never issue refunds or modify customer records automatically. Escalate to a person when needed.

brief.application: Use Azure for this synthetic architecture qualification. Assist support staff using a synthetic ticket queue, approved knowledge and customer records from an existing CRM. Include authorized retrieval, grounded answer drafting, a staff interface and human escalation. Never issue refunds or modify customer records automatically. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

lastAsked.question: Where do the files live, and roughly how many are there?
lastAsked.beginner: For example “SharePoint and a shared drive, about 20,000 files”.

requirements.statement: The assistant must never issue refunds or create, update or delete CRM records. It only drafts, and those actions go to a person.
requirements.rationale: An automated refund or record change would cause direct financial or data-integrity harm.
requirements.basis: User: "Never issue refunds or modify customer records automatically."

requirements.statement: Retrieval returns only approved knowledge the signed-in staff member is permitted to see. If the identity or groups are unknown, it returns nothing.
requirements.rationale: Without per-user filtering, staff could see restricted content in drafts.

requirements.statement: Each draft cites its source passages. When the evidence is insufficient, the assistant abstains and offers escalation. (Proposal: the target is to be agreed.)
requirements.rationale: Ungrounded answers could mislead customers. Abstaining plus human escalation limits that risk.
requirements.basis: User: "grounded answer drafting ... and human escalation"

decisions.subject: design.azure-support-staff-knowledge-assistant-first-sketch
decisions.title: Azure support-staff knowledge assistant (first sketch)
decisions.context: Scope: the full support assistant flow on Azure, covering staff sign-in, a staff web app, an orchestration API, read-only CRM lookup, the synthetic ticket queue, an approved knowledge store and a permission-filtered search index, Azure OpenAI for drafting, a grounding/safety check, human escalation and monitoring. Assumptions: Entra ID sign-in, the region, model deployment and subscription access are all unverified and still open. The CRM connection is read-only, and the assistant has no refund or record-write path. Every component here is design-only; no native Azure generator covers this workload yet, so building it needs engineering work.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.
